BLOCK B
Ember · a company, almost
AI OFF

A STORY THAT HAPPENS EVERY WEEK, EVERYWHERE

In October, three friends — Lena, Marco and Priya — agree to start a venture. They call it Ember. They
open a group chat, split the roles, and shake hands on equal thirds. In November, a supplier offers Lena
favourable terms if she commits before month-end; she signs a supply order worth 40,000 — signature
block: "Lena Vasseur, for Ember." In December the three register Ember as a company, everything by the
book. In January the goods arrive and the business opens. By March, half the order is paid, the
company's account holds 1,200, and the supplier writes asking who, precisely, will be paying the rest.

Lena says: "The company owes it — the order
was always for Ember." Marco says: "We never
approved that order, and in November there
was no company to approve anything." The
supplier says: "Somebody signed. Somebody
owes." Who is right — and does it matter that
everyone acted in good faith?

Push further: in November, was there any
"Ember" at all — and if not, what exactly did
Lena's signature do?

— No answer is handed to you. Argue it from your reading; be ready to defend where you land.

有人 欠的。”谁是对的——这重要吗？每个人都真诚地行事吗？更进一步：11月，有没有 到底是“Ember”——如果不是，那到底是什么 莉娜的签名呢？——没有答案给你。从你的阅读中论证它；准备好保卫你所在的地方。第 2 周 · Ember · 开场 3

pages.english:
BLOCK B
Four moves, and the last one is a decision
AI OFF

THE METHOD, INSTALLED

Actor. Form. Liability. Then decide — with conditions.

Every entity dispute in this course, including the ten your boards open after the break, is

worked in the same four moves. Last week you argued from chairs; this week the chairs

get a method.

1 · Name the actor

Who did this — a person, the
company, or an organ of it? A
signatory is not always the
company.

2 · Fit the form

What does this company's
form, under its own national
law, actually permit here —
and in which document does
the rule live?

3 · Place the liability

When paper and behaviour
disagree, somebody absorbs
the loss. Say who, and what
rule puts it there.

4 · Decide, with

conditions

The board's decision — and
the ratification, amendment
or verification that must
come with it.

WHY THE ORDER MATTERS

Move 1 is the move everyone skips: "the company decided" is a sentence that hides three questions — which

organ, with what power, carried by whose signature. A board that starts at Move 3 is arguing about a loss

before it knows whose act created it.

THE RULE THIS WEEK RUNS ON

Companies are persons the law builds, and the formalities are the construction. Everything a company can

do for you — own, owe, shield, survive — it does because the paperwork is load-bearing. Today you will read

ten files in which somebody treated one formality as decoration.

pages.english:
MOVE 1 · NAME THE ACTOR
What your reading gives you
AI OFF

BEFORE THE BIRTH, NOBODY IS HOME

Registration is constitutive. Before it, "the company"
is a hope with a logo.

FROM YOUR READINGA company exists from its register entry or certificate — not from the founders' agreement, the name,
or the intention. A person who signs for a company not yet formed is, by default everywhere, personally bound: a non-
existent principal can grant no authority, so the signature holds the signer. The traditions then differ on the cure — how,
once born, the company may adopt or assume the obligation, and through which organ.

In the story

"For Ember," signed in November; Ember born in
December; goods delivered to and half-paid by the
company in January.

The reading

November's actor is Lena — the only legal person at
the table. The open question is whether the
company's later conduct (taking delivery, part-
paying) amounts to assumption under its own law,
and whether whoever performed that conduct had
the power to assume anything.

Civil bank

Code systems typically provide an express
mechanism: the acting person is liable; the company
may take over the obligation after registration, with
formalities. Certainty by procedure.

Common bank

Case-grown answers: the signer is bound; a company
cannot "ratify" an act done before it existed, so a
fresh adoption — a new contract on the old terms, or
conduct amounting to one — is required. Certainty by
doctrine.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART

Both banks protect the supplier by holding Lena — the person who chose to sign early. The law's sympathy for

good-faith enthusiasm is real, and it is expressed as a rule about who pays for it.

第 1 步 · 命名演员 你的阅读内容让你关闭人工智能 出生前，没人在家 注册是构成性的。之前的“公司” 是一个带有标志的希望。根据您的阅读，公司的存在来自于其注册条目或证书，而不是来自创始人的协议、名称、 或意图。

与尚未成立的公司签约的人，默认情况下在任何地方都受个人约束：非 现有的校长不能授予任何权力，因此签名保留签名者。传统在治疗上有所不同——如何， 一旦诞生，公司可能会通过哪个机构来承担义务。故事里 《For Ember》于 11 月签署；

Ember 诞生于 十二月；货物交付至并由其支付一半费用 一月份的公司。阅读 十一月的演员是莉娜——这里唯一的合法人物 该表。悬而未决的问题是是否 公司后期行为（提货、部分- 支付）相当于根据其自己的法律承担， 以及实施该行为的人是否 承担任何事情的权力。

民间银行 代码系统通常提供一个express 机制：行为人责任；公司 注册后可以接管义务， 手续。程序的确定性。共同银行 案例得出的答案：签名者的约束；

陪伴 不能“批准”一项在其存在之前所做的行为，因此 新采用——按照旧条款签订新合同，或者 行为相当于一——是必需的。确定性 学说。不舒服的部分 两家银行都通过持有莉娜（选择提前签约的人）来保护供应商。

法律的同情 真诚的热情是真实存在的，它表现为关于谁为此付费的规则。第 2 周 · 动作 1 · 阅读 6

MOVE 2 · FIT THE FORM
Ember · February
AI OFF

FROM THE FILE

December's registration used the registry's standard constitution — nobody changed a word, nobody
read one either. The three founders did agree something, in the group chat, the same week: "rule for us
three: nothing over 10k without all of us signing off." In February the supplier offered a renewal at triple
volume, one week only. Lena — the only founder in the office — signed it alone: "Ember, by Lena
Vasseur, director." This time the company existed, and this time Marco's objection is different: "We had a
rule. It's in writing. She broke it." Lena's answer: "The rule is in a chat. My name is on the register."

Two documents claim to govern: the
constitution they filed and never read, and the
pact they wrote and never filed. Which one
decides whether the company is bound — and
which one decides whether Lena is in trouble?

The supplier saw neither document. Should
that matter? Should it matter more or less
than it did in November?

Push further: the founders had a real
agreement, made in good faith, and it may
govern nothing that counts. What would they
have had to do to make their rule real — and
why does the law demand that extra step?

— The reading follows. Notice that your instinct about which document "should" win is your tradition
speaking.

MOVE 2 · FIT THE FORM
What your reading gives you
AI OFF

THE RULE IS ONLY AS STRONG AS THE DOCUMENT IT LIVES IN

Constitution, statute, private pact — three homes for a
rule, three completely different powers.

FROM YOUR READINGA company's constitution binds the company and every member; a private agreement binds only its
signatories; and the statute's defaults govern everything the founders never wrote — which, for founders who adopt a
standard constitution unread, is nearly everything. The internal/external line then does the rest: rules about approval live
inside; the power to bind outsiders is decided by the register (civil bank) or by authority and its appearance (common bank).

In the story

A filed constitution nobody read; a 10k rule in a chat;
a register naming Lena a director; a supplier that saw
only the signature.

The reading

The chat pact is, at best, an informal shareholders'
agreement: real between the three, invisible to the
company's constitution and to the world. The
renewal's fate turns on what the unread constitution
and the statute's defaults gave a single director — not
on the rule the founders believed in.

Civil bank

If the register shows Lena with power of
representation, the company is bound; the 10k rule
operates inward only. The register is the promise
strangers may trust.

Common bank

A sole director signing in the ordinary course carries
actual or apparent authority; outsiders may assume

cannot see it. The fix was always available: write the rule into the constitution. It costs one filing, and this

morning it would have been priceless.

enough, what was the shield for?

What your reading gives you

THE SHIELD HOLDS — AND THE DIRECT ROUTES GO AROUND IT

Nobody needs to break the veil to reach the person
who actually acted.

FROM YOUR READINGLimited liability means members risk their contribution — Priya's sentence is good law. Courts set
personality aside only narrowly: fraud, evasion, pure façade. But most recovery never touches the veil, because the law
offers direct routes: the person who signed before the birth is personally bound; the company is bound by acts within its
representatives' external power; and the insider who broke an internal rule answers inward, to the company itself.

In the story

November: Lena signed for a company that did not
exist. February: a registered director signed within
her external power. March: an empty account and
three theories of fairness.

The reading

November's debt sits on Lena unless the company
validly assumed it. February's debt sits on the
company — thin account and all — with a live inward
question against Lena for breaking the 10k pact.
Marco and Priya keep the shield: no fraud, no façade,
no signature.

In the story

The supplier: "somewhere in that arrangement is my
money."

The reading

Partly true, and precisely mapped: some of it is with
Lena, some with a company that cannot pay yet,
none with the two who only contributed. Suppliers
who dislike that map have always had the answer the
law leaves open — ask for a guarantee before
delivering. Watch that thought: it returns in eight
minutes.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART

The placement is coherent and it still leaves an unpaid supplier facing a shielded majority. The law has chosen

its loser and can say why. Whether the choice is right is Week 1's question, permanently open — and your

board sits inside it all term.

The supplier proposes, in writing, open for one week: it will release Lena personally from the November

counter. Not a mood — a decision, with the
conditions attached that make it survivable.

MOVE 4 · DECIDE, WITH CONDITIONS
What a built decision looks like
AI OFF

A DECISION IS AN ACT PLUS ITS CONDITIONS

Anyone can say "accept." A board says accept — on
these terms, after these steps, with this cured.

The decision

Counter: take the renewal cut and Lena's release;
accept exclusivity at one year with volumes tied to
actual sales; refuse blanket personal guarantees —
offer instead a single guarantee capped at the
November balance, from Lena alone, expiring on
payment.

Why that shape

November is Lena's exposure; her capped guarantee
prices her own early signature without re-exposing
the two who kept the rules. Blanket guarantees from
all three would quietly repeal the company form —
the one thing the founders bought in December.

The conditions

Before signature: the company formally assumes the
November order through the proper organ, so its
status stops being arguable. Alongside it: the 10k rule
moves from the chat into the constitution, and
signing authority above the threshold becomes two-
founder. The file's cause, cured in the file's own
settlement.

The defence question

Every decision must answer: would this morning's
offer have been made at all if your conditions had
been in place from the start? Here — with a real
signing rule and a properly assumed order, the
supplier would have had no lever for blanket
guarantees. That is what "conditions cure the failure"
means.

BOTH BANKS, ONE LESSON

Nothing in this decision needed exotic law. Assumption formalities differ by tradition; the governance cure —

put the rule where the law can see it — is identical on both banks. When a cure is tradition-proof, it is usually

the right one.

CARRY THIS INTO YOUR OWN FILE

Every board's dossier ends with an offer that arrived this morning — and every offer carries one term that

outlives the dispute. Price the headline, then find that term. Your decision, with conditions, is the deliverable of

the day.

pages.english:
BLOCK B
Where the argument lands
AI OFF

THE WEEK'S JUDGMENT QUESTION

The company form protects whom — from whom?

Both readings are true at once, and running a company means holding both. The form is

a shield for the people inside it and a set of promises to the people outside it — and

every protection on one side is priced to the other.

The shield reading

Limited liability exists so that ordinary people can
attempt enterprise without betting their homes.

Marco and Priya kept every rule and owe nothing
more — that is the system working, not a loophole.

Remove the shield and only the already-rich, or the
reckless, start companies.

The promises reading

The shield is purchased with formalities: real
registration, real capital, real organs, a register
strangers can trust.

The supplier's guarantee demand is the market
repricing a shield the founders wanted for free.

Skip the formalities and the law's sympathy moves
outside — to the person who trusted the paperwork.

THE HONEST TENSION

Ember's founders wanted the shield's protection and the chat's informality, and the whole story is the bill for

wanting both. A board that cannot say which promises its own company has actually kept — formalities

observed, organs real, register accurate — does not yet know what its shield is worth.

CARRY THIS INTO YOUR OWN FILE

In every one of the ten dossiers, the form worked and somebody's use of it failed. Your board's first question

after the break is not "what happened to us?" — it is "which of our promises was theatre?"

AI enters, as research assistant
AI ON · DECLARED ROLE

THIS WEEK'S DECLARED ROLE

Research assistant. It maps the rules of your
company's form. It does not make your board's
decision — and it will offer to.

USE IT FOR

The rules

What law creates your form; what it
says about the mechanism in your
file; which organ or person could
validly have done the act — and what
follows because it was done anyway.

DISTRUST IT ON

Jurisdiction

Company law is national law, and the
tool answers in a Delaware or London
accent. For most of this room, that
accent is wrong. Make it say where
each rule is true, and for which form.

NEVER ACCEPT

A verdict

The questions arrive later, on paper,
in postures the tool has never seen. If
it volunteers a recommendation,
write it down and keep it — you will
be asked where you disagreed.

THE HABIT BEGINS — AND IT IS HANDED IN

Ask AI, then disagree: the handwritten paragraph (150–200 words), announced last week, due today,

individually assessed. What you asked, what it said, where your judgement departed from it.

NEW WITH IT · THE JURISDICTION LINE

One running line, kept as you go, in your own hand: every proposition the tool states as fact, tagged with the

country and the legal form it is true for. A rule of company law that has lost its jurisdiction is not a rule — it is a

rumour. One of the questions you have not seen yet asks you to read your line back against your own answer.

THE DIAGRAM CHANGES THE QUESTION

Week 1's dilemma was moral. Week 2's machinery
decides who is even entitled to answer it.

Move 1 · the actor

The discharge is the subsidiary's act, done by its
organs under its licence. "Northwind pollutes" was
Week 1's shorthand; the file behind it names a local
company with its own board — and a parent whose
act, so far, is only ownership.

Move 2 · the form

The subsidiary's board runs its operations and owes
its duties to its company; the parent, as shareholder,
holds the shareholder's levers — appoint, remove,
resolve, instruct where the constitution allows. The
parent can cause the standard to change; it must do
it through the organs, not around them.

Move 3 · the liability

Salomon runs between companies too: the parent is
not automatically liable for the subsidiary's lawful
operations. But the shield has a known pressure
point — a parent that takes over direction of the
specific conduct, or publicly assumes responsibility
for group standards, can acquire duties of its own.
Control is a dial, and liability tends to follow the hand
on it.

The letter, re-read

Addressed to "the board of Northwind" — a body that
does not exist. That is not a defect in the manager's
courage; it is the diagram doing what diagrams do:
diffusing responsibility until nobody's inbox owns it.
Move 4 exists to put a name back on it.

THE TRAP ON BOTH BANKS

The legal reading tempts a clean conclusion: the parent is shielded, the subsidiary is compliant, file closed.

Notice what that conclusion quietly decides — that the diagram answers the conscience question. Week 1

already showed you it does not. The law places the liability; it has never yet placed the responsibility.

WALKTHROUGH · THE DECISION
A decision with conditions — built in the

open

BY HAND · AI
OFF

TO JUDGE AGAINST, NOT TO REQUIRE

The decision, built twice — because there are two
defensible answers and choosing between them is the
decision.

Route A · adopt the home standard, group-

wide

The parent board resolves a single discharge
standard for the group — the stricter one — and
instructs through the organs: shareholder resolution,
subsidiary board adoption, then the work.
Conditions: a phased timetable with dated
milestones; funded budget before announcement;
independent verification of each phase; the junior
manager answered in writing, by name, by the parent
board.

Route B · keep local compliance, govern it

honestly

The subsidiary continues within its permit — and the
group stops hiding behind the diagram. Conditions:
independent monitoring published on a schedule; a
defined trigger (evidence of downstream harm, or
regulatory movement in either country) that forces
Route A automatically; the decision minuted at
parent level, owned, and reviewed annually.

Which one, and why

Route A is the one to take. Not because the law
requires it — it does not — but because Route B's
honest version is barely cheaper: real monitoring,
real triggers and real ownership cost most of what
compliance-plus costs, while keeping the risk that the
trigger fires late. When the honest version of the easy
option costs nearly the hard option, the hard option
is the bargain.

Notice what both routes share

Conditions with dates, money and organs attached. A
"decision" without them is a press release. And in
both, the decision is owned at the parent — the one
thing the diagram was letting everyone avoid.

THE DEFENCE QUESTION EVERY BOARD ANSWERS

If your conditions had been in place from the start, what would this morning have looked like — and would

the letter ever have needed writing? Carry that question into your own file: it is printed on your page.

Week 2 · Business Entities & Formation
AI OFF

WHAT YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO DO NOW

Read any signature and know, before anyone argues,
which person it bound — and read any company and
know which of its promises are real.

MOVE 1

"The company decided" hides three questions — which organ,
with what power, carried by whose signature. Before
registration, nobody is home, and the signer pays for the hope.

MOVE 2

A rule is only as strong as its document. Constitutions bind
companies and every future holder; private pacts bind their
signers; the statute's defaults govern everything nobody
wrote.

MOVE 3

The veil holds, narrowly and on purpose — and the direct
routes go around it: the early signer, the bound company, the
insider who answers inward. The law chooses its losers and
can say why.

MOVE 4

A decision is an act plus conditions — the ratification, the
amendment, the verification, each with a date and an organ.
Judged by one question: would this morning have happened
at all?

YOUR BOARD CHALLENGE, BEFORE WE MEET AGAIN

Your company's legal skeleton is now fixed by its file. Its face is yours to build. As a board, decide three things

and bring them in writing next week: the trade name your company will actually go to market under, the one

trademark you would register first to protect it, and the flagship product or service it leads with. One page,

signed by the whole board. Take it seriously — Week 3 tests that product against its first regulator, and

everything you invent tonight will be lived with all term.

THE THREAD TO WEEK 3

Today built the person. Next week the person meets the state: Regulation & Compliance — who is allowed to

sell what, to whom, under whose watch. Bring your product. The regulator is already waiting for it.
